data.body:
Plan authored and reviewed to PASS (0 blocking, 1 minor P6 advisory), 1 round, signed at HEAD 1052bc856f.

All three reported reproductions CONFIRMED verbatim on this tree by running the functions:
models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0") -> the three bare Anthropic rungs;
largest_window_tokens(same) -> 1000000; models_at_or_above("anthropic:claude-opus-4-8") ->
["claude-opus-4-8"]. Mechanism confirmed at sizing.py:319-327 (fallthrough at :327) and
sizing.py:137-146 (:146).

Two corrections to the original problem statement, both folded into the plan:
- 7de4 is NOT on origin/main. `_rung_target` and tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py are both
  absent at HEAD 1052bc856f (7de4 is committed on the unpushed branch feat/7de4-rung-target).
  The plan is therefore written entirely against main and names no 7de4 symbol; the only overlap
  is 7de4s nova start-rung pinning test, which whichever change lands second must update.
- A SECOND call site has the same defect: prerequisites.py:260-261 takes ladder[0] for an
  unlocated primary, so prerequisite-coverage escalation also downgrades and crosses providers.
  The planned models_at_or_above change fixes it without editing that file (its existing
  except (ValueError, IndexError) at :262 turns the resulting IndexError into the explicit
  input-too-large indeterminate at :263). Pinned by a new test rather than assumed.

Separate defect found, NOT ticketed: MODEL_LADDER (sizing.py:99-103) lists claude-sonnet-4-6 and
claude-opus-4-8 at the SAME 1000000 window, so the sonnet -> opus escalation rung buys no extra
context at all. A context-limit escalation that gains zero window is a guaranteed second failure
plus opus pricing. Worth its own ticket.
